principle_text: When the persuadee is engaged in casual, non-donation-related conversation, avoid responding with only small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows unfamiliarity with a charity, avoid assuming prior knowledge or immediately asking for donations without first providing clear, engaging information about the cause.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or unrelated personal information, avoid sharing unrelated personal details that do not advance the donation conversation.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about a charity, avoid vague or indirect introductions that do not clearly explain the charity's purpose or impact.
When the persuadee shows limited but uncertain knowledge about a charity, avoid assuming full awareness or pushing for immediate commitment without first clarifying their understanding.
When the persuadee shares routine activities without expressing interest in the cause, avoid focusing solely on personal anecdotes that do not connect to the charitable mission.
When the persuadee shares personal interests unrelated to the charity, avoid focusing solely on those interests without connecting them back to the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows openness or a positive attitude toward charitable giving, you should directly engage them with questions about their donation habits to encourage further discussion.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or unrelated comments, avoid sharing personal details that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows curiosity or limited knowledge about a charity, you should introduce the charity by name and invite them to learn more to foster engagement and openness to donation.
When the persuadee signals openness to discussing a donation, avoid giving neutral or non-committal responses that fail to advance the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee responds positively to casual conversation, avoid staying on unrelated topics that do not guide the discussion toward the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee responds with enthusiasm about a casual topic, avoid staying on unrelated small talk that does not guide the conversation toward the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee responds with unrelated small talk, avoid merely reciprocating without steering the conversation back to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee responds with casual, unrelated topics, avoid continuing small talk that does not guide the conversation toward the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee responds with casual, positive small talk, avoid continuing unrelated chit-chat without steering the conversation toward the charitable cause or donation request.
When the persuadee shares neutral or casual information about their day, avoid responding with similarly neutral or unrelated comments that do not advance the donation conversation.
When the persuadee expresses familiarity but questions the charity's efficiency, avoid assuming acceptance without providing clear, credible information to address their concerns.
When the persuadee shows familiarity with a charity, avoid simply naming the organization without adding compelling reasons or unique information to increase their willingness to donate.
When the persuadee responds with a question unrelated to the charity or donation, avoid continuing only with small talk that does not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about your personal life, avoid sharing unrelated personal details that do not connect to the charitable cause or encourage donation.
When the persuadee shares personal work details, avoid shifting the conversation to unrelated personal job descriptions that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee is unfamiliar with the charity, avoid assuming prior knowledge and instead provide clear, engaging information to build awareness and interest.
When the persuadee expresses donating non-monetary items, avoid assuming they are ready to make monetary donations without further exploration of their motivations and preferences.
